extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, practitioners subject to USPTO discipline, and USPTO OED/enforcement staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal discipline on a USPTO-registered practitioner based on state disciplinary action under 37 C.F.R. §11.24, including service, response deadlines, applicability of new rules, and publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct — 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h) of the rules, it is professional misconduct for a practitioner to be publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order predicates reciprocal discipline upon a State Bar public reproof. Example on this page: Mr. Gortler was publicly reproved by the State Bar Court of California in connection with his guilty plea and conviction of a misdemeanor (Cal. Penal Code §243(e)(1) - spousal battery). The misconduct therefore qualifies as professional misconduct under §11.804(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose reciprocal discipline — 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Deputy General Counsel (OED Director) may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting that the Acting Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office initiated disciplinary proceedings pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24; the Notice and Order informed the Respondent of the Complaint and requested imposition of discipline identical to the State Bar's discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to oppose and 40‑day response deadline — 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service must be proper (see certified mailing and delivery below). Failure to file a timely response allows the Director to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and to impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice requirements (certified mailing and delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order must be served — in this case it was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. provided) and was delivered to Respondent on a specified date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents the mailing (certified mail receipt number) and delivery date (March 2, 2013) as proof of service; proper service is a prerequisite to the deadline and to any later finding of no genuine issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond — finding of no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Respondent fails to file a response within the allotted time, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and that reciprocal discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states that because Respondent did not file a response within forty days, reprimand was appropriate. This illustrates the procedural consequence of non-response in reciprocal-discipline proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation under new disciplinary rules — 37 C.F.R. §11.901(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplinary proceeding initiated prior to the effective date of new disciplinary rules may be continued under the new rules if the conduct at issue would continue to justify disciplinary action under the new rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Agency initiated proceedings under earlier rules (e.g., §10.23(b)(6)), the Order explains that the change to new rules (effective May 3, 2013) does not prevent continuation because the conduct remains sanctionable under §11.804(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of discipline identical to state discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Acting Director may order discipline identical to that imposed by the State Bar where appropriate (reciprocal discipline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice sought 'reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the State Bar Court of California.' Where no genuine factual dispute exists, the Office imposed a reprimand corresponding to the State's public reproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and posting of disciplinary action — Official Gazette and OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is required to publish a Notice in the Official Gazette and disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are to be posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the text of the Notice of Reprimand and cites authority (35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §11.24) for publication and public posting. This establishes transparency and public notice as part of the remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director compliance with other procedural rules — 37 C.F.R. §11.59 and further relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is directed to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.59 and to direct such other and further relief as the nature of the cause shall require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order does not detail §11.59 on this page, it instructs OED to follow applicable procedural provisions and to take any additional actions required by the nature of the case.
